The test image shows a **leaf** with a whitish/grayish powdery coating spread across the upper surface. The leaf is still mostly green but has diffuse white powdery patches — strongly suggestive of Powdery Mildew.

Now I'll view one reference image from Powdery_Mildew to confirm.

The reference image shows white powdery circular spots on tomato leaves — consistent with Powdery Mildew. The test image shows a more advanced/diffuse stage where the white powdery coating has spread and merged across the leaf surface, which matches the KB description: "spots that begin small but expand and converge."

The broad, oval leaf shape in the test image may reflect a different leaf position or variety, but the key diagnostic feature — white powdery sporulation on the leaf surface — is clear and consistent with Powdery Mildew. No concentric rings (Early Blight), no brown lesions, no yellow halos, no velvety mold on underside (Leaf Mold).
